pll1d19c8-d1e3477.summary: With Augustine, the divine essence is not the matter of the persons, as three statues made from the same gold are called one gold. Among equal statues there is more gold in three than in one; in the Trinity this is not so. So the three persons are not one essence by material cause.
claims: The divine essence is not a common matter of the persons.
In the Trinity three persons are not more essence than one.
The persons are not one essence by material cause.

pl-l1d19c8.summary: Adds with Augustine that the divine essence is not the matter of the three persons, as three gold statues are one gold. In equal statues there is more gold in three than in one; in the Trinity this is in no way so. So the three persons are not one essence by material cause.
claims: The divine essence is not the matter of the three persons.
Three statues contain more gold than one; three persons are not more essence than one.
The persons are not one essence by material causality.
